prompt: Stage 3-1, level 6 with 38 gold, 79 HP, on a 2-loss streak that costs you about 6 HP a round. Your board is 2-starred everywhere except a 1-star 3-cost carry. The shop has nothing. You have rolled twice each of the last three rounds "to look for the carry". What is the correct habit here?

options.label: Roll twice again: you only need one more copy
Stop rolling entirely. Bank to 50, accept the 6 HP losses, and roll once with purpose at a planned point
Level to 7 now to raise 3-cost odds

explanation:
Two rolls a round at level 6 is 4 gold a round, and over the four rounds from 3-1 to 3-5 that is 16 gold plus the interest those 16 gold would have earned: you arrive at 4-1 with roughly 25 gold less than the player who did nothing. For that price you bought eight shops at 25% 3-cost odds, each shop with a 5-slot chance of one specific unit out of a pool of thirteen 3-costs. The expected number of copies found is under one. You are paying a full level's worth of gold for a coin flip on a single 2-star.

The 6 HP a round is real but affordable at 79 HP: four more losses leaves you at 55, still above every threshold that matters at 4-1. What is not affordable is entering stage 4 with 25 gold when the 4-2 rolldown is where the actual carry upgrade lives at 10% 4-cost and 43% 3-cost odds at level 7. Bank, level at 4-1, and roll at 4-2 with 50+. Leveling to 7 now spends 18 gold for slightly better odds on a board that cannot afford to roll at all.
principle: Rolling a little each round is the most expensive habit in Emerald: it spends the rolldown before the rolldown.
commonMistake: Believing a small roll is cheap because it is only 2 gold. The cost is the compound interest and the rolldown you no longer have.
